## Root cause proven, fix committed (not yet pushed)

**Commit:** `206125736d` on `fix/12e4-fetch-abort` (worktree `/Users/joeoakhart/fix/12e4-fetch-abort`).

### Proven root cause

`_fetch_origin` built its git argv with no `http.lowSpeedLimit` / `http.lowSpeedTime`, so git's curl handle had no throughput-keyed abort and a connection that was established but moved zero bytes was bounded only by the wall-clock `subprocess.run(timeout=_GIT_TIMEOUT)` at 300s.

### Discriminating experiment (local listener, no paid calls)

| scenario | config | result |
|---|---|---|
| stall, 0 B/s | none (before) | still running at the 45s harness cap |
| stall, 0 B/s | limit=1000, time=5 | aborts **5.1s**, `Operation too slow` |
| stall, 0 B/s | limit=1000, time=2 | aborts **2.1s** |
| dribble 2000 B/s, 60s | limit=1000, time=5 | **not aborted** |
| dribble 4000 B/s, 20s | limit=1000, time=2 | **not aborted** (fails later as `transfer closed`) |

Real-remote safety: 5 warm fetches (0.4-0.6s) and **3 cold full clones of the 80 MB mirror at 87.8 / 88.4 / 101.4s** all complete under limit=1000 / time=10. A legitimately slow 90-second transfer is not aborted.

### Replication through the real entry point

`resolve_ref` against a wedged remote: **30.2s** (3 attempts x 10s) vs the 300s ceiling.

### Mutation evidence (both directions)

- Drop the low-speed args (re-seed the exact root cause) -> stall test + argv test RED.
- Force attempts to 1 -> retry test RED.
- Raise the floor 100000x so the abort is effectively wall-time-keyed -> **the slow-but-progressing test goes RED**. This is the one that matters: it proves the discriminator would catch the failure mode that is worse than the bug.
- Refactoring litmus: renamed 4 internals (`argv`, `attempts`, `floor`, `window`) -> all 4 still pass. Not change-detector tests.

### Forced module split

`repo_snapshot.py` was 788/800 LOC, so the fix could not land without splitting. The git-subprocess + fetch-locking cluster moved whole into `_snapshot/git_fetch.py` along the seam it already formed. 788 -> 610; new module 326. Dependency is one-directional.

### Sibling sweep

Three other 300s network fetches share the exposure and are filed as 851e-19ef-31dd-4e38 (`discovered_from` this ticket): `review_bot/gerrit_client.py:367`, `opcert_service/workspace.py:107,124`, `_commands/init.py:398,419`. Left out of this change deliberately.

### Gates

`make lint` exit 0, `make typecheck` exit 0. Full suite re-running on the clean tree.

NOT pushed to Gerrit; ticket left open per instruction.

compiled_state.description:
# Abort a stalled review-bot `git fetch` in seconds instead of burning the 300s budget

## Context / Problem

Bug `df2c-e4b8-496d-4698` proved the review bot's per-review `git fetch` of the GitHub mirror
intermittently hangs: 25 consecutive runs in `compose-review-bot-1` produced 2 hangs past 320s
(rc=124) against a 1-3s median on an 80 MB / 54k-object repo.

Root cause (confirmed by experiment, see below): `_fetch_origin` in
`src/rebar/_snapshot/repo_snapshot.py` builds its git argv with no `http.lowSpeedLimit` /
`http.lowSpeedTime`, so git's curl handle has **no throughput-keyed abort**. A byte-starved
connection is bounded only by the wall-clock `subprocess.run(timeout=_GIT_TIMEOUT)` at 300s.

Change `0347` already removed the DURABLE damage (a retryable coverage gap now defers the vote
instead of casting `LLM-Review -1`, escalating only after a 3-attempt budget). It does **not**
shorten the stall: each stalled review still costs 5 minutes, and three unlucky stalls in a row
still lose the review. This ticket makes the stall abort in seconds. It does **not** touch
`voter.py`'s retryable-gap logic.

## Measured evidence

Against a local listener that accepts the connection, sends HTTP headers, then sends zero body
bytes (a true stall), and a second listener that dribbles 2000 B/s continuously (legitimately
slow but progressing):

| scenario | git config | result |
|---|---|---|
| stall (0 B/s) | none (today) | still running at the 45s harness cap; would burn 300s |
| stall (0 B/s) | `lowSpeedLimit=1000`, `lowSpeedTime=5` | aborts at **5.1s**, rc=128, "Operation too slow" |
| dribble 2000 B/s for 60s | `lowSpeedLimit=1000`, `lowSpeedTime=5` | **not aborted** — runs to the harness cap, still transferring |

Real-world safety check against the actual GitHub mirror with `lowSpeedLimit=1000`,
`lowSpeedTime=10`: 5 warm fetches (0.4-0.6s) and 3 **cold full clones of the whole 80 MB repo
(87.8s / 88.4s / 101.4s)** all completed — a legitimately slow 90-second transfer is not aborted.

## Approach

1. Pass `-c http.lowSpeedLimit=<bytes/s> -c http.lowSpeedTime=<seconds>` on the snapshot fetch,
   so a byte-starved connection aborts on **throughput**, not wall time. Defaults 1000 B/s over
   10s (evidence above); both overridable by env for operators on pathological links.
2. Retry the fetch in-process a bounded number of times when — and only when — it failed with a
   low-speed abort, so a transient stall self-heals inside the same review instead of deferring
   to a backfill pass. Worst case becomes ~3x10s rather than 300s.

### Module-size constraint (why this change also moves code)

`src/rebar/_snapshot/repo_snapshot.py` is **788 LOC against the hard 800 cap**
(`.github/module-size-limit.txt`), leaving no room. Per the module-size policy the fix splits
along a call-graph seam that already exists: the git-subprocess + fetch-locking cluster
(`_interprocess_lock`, `_fetch_lock_for`, `_git`, `_has_remote`, `_rev_parse`,
`_is_auth_failure`, `_fetch_origin`, the `Snapshot*Error` vocabulary they raise, and the
`_AUTH_STDERR_MARKERS` they classify with) moves whole into a new sibling
`src/rebar/_snapshot/git_fetch.py`. The dependency becomes one-directional
(`repo_snapshot` -> `git_fetch`); no behaviour moves with it, and `_snapshot/__init__.py`'s
public surface is unchanged.

## Scope

In scope:
- `src/rebar/_snapshot/git_fetch.py` (new — extracted plumbing + the stall abort and retry)
- `src/rebar/_snapshot/repo_snapshot.py` (extraction; call sites re-pointed)
- `tests/unit/` — new test module for the stall-abort behaviour

Explicitly out of scope: `src/rebar/review_bot/voter.py` (0347's retryable-gap logic),
`src/rebar/llm/*`, and the 300s `_GIT_TIMEOUT` ceiling itself, which stays as the outer bound.

## Testing

RED-first, and deliberately **not** asserting on wall-clock durations (they flake in CI):

- A test that spawns a real local listener which accepts and then sends **zero bytes**, points
  a fetch at it, and asserts the fetch fails with a low-speed abort well inside a short bound —
  RED today (the fetch is only bounded by the 300s ceiling).
- A test that spawns a listener **dribbling bytes continuously below normal speed but above the
  configured floor**, and asserts the fetch is **not** aborted — this is the discriminator that
  stops the fix from killing healthy slow clones, and it fails if the threshold is keyed on wall
  time rather than throughput.
- A test asserting the emitted git argv carries the low-speed options (cheap contract guard).
- A test asserting a low-speed abort is retried the configured number of times and a
  non-low-speed failure (e.g. auth) is **not** retried.

Mutation check both directions: removing the low-speed args must return the stall test to RED,
and a behaviour-preserving rename must not break any of them.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A stalled fetch (a remote that accepts the connection and sends no bytes) aborts in ~10
      seconds rather than at the 300s ceiling, demonstrated by a reproduction against an
      unresponsive local remote.
- [ ] A genuinely slow-but-progressing fetch is **not** aborted; the threshold is keyed on
      throughput, not wall time, and is proven so by a dribbling-remote test.
- [ ] A transient low-speed abort is retried in-process a bounded number of times, so the common
      case still produces a real review; a non-low-speed failure (auth, bad ref) is not retried.
- [ ] `voter.py`'s retryable-gap logic from change 0347 is untouched.
- [ ] `src/rebar/_snapshot/repo_snapshot.py` and the new `git_fetch.py` are each under the 800
      LOC module-size cap.
- [ ] `make lint`, `make typecheck`, and the default test selection all pass (exit 0).

file_impact.reason: New sibling module. The git-subprocess + fetch-locking cluster extracted whole from repo_snapshot.py along the call-graph seam it already formed there (that file was 788/800 LOC, leaving no room for the fix). Carries the new throughput-keyed stall abort (stall_abort_args -> http.lowSpeedLimit/lowSpeedTime), is_stall_abort, and the bounded in-process retry that repeats a stall and only a stall.

Source of the extraction: 788 -> 610 LOC. Call sites re-pointed at git_fetch; a _fetch_lock_path() helper keeps the store layout here so the lower layer needs no import back. Also arms the stall abort on the SECOND network fetch in _ensure_blobs_present, which had the same 300s exposure.
Imported _interprocess_lock from repo_snapshot; re-pointed to git_fetch.interprocess_lock. Import-only change, no behaviour.

Regenerated by scripts/gen_env_registry.py for the three new knobs (REBAR_SNAPSHOT_STALL_FLOOR_BYTES_PER_SEC / _WINDOW_SECONDS / _ATTEMPTS). The generator scrapes literal os.environ reads, so the helper takes the already-read value and each call site names its variable verbatim.

New RED-first tests. A real local listener that accepts and sends zero bytes must fail as a stall and not as a wall-clock timeout; a listener dribbling bytes continuously must NOT be aborted (the throughput-vs-wall-time discriminator); the fetch argv carries the low-speed options; only a stall is retried.
_is_auth_failure moved to git_fetch.is_auth_failure; reference re-pointed. Assertions unchanged.
The credential-prompt spy patched repo_snapshot._git, now repo_snapshot.git_run (the binding _materialize_tree actually calls). Assertions unchanged.
monkeypatch.setattr target renamed _interprocess_lock -> interprocess_lock after the move. Assertions unchanged.
monkeypatch.setattr target renamed _has_remote -> has_remote after the move. Assertions unchanged.
